title: 1952 AHSME Problem 48
statement: Two cyclists, \(k\) miles apart, and starting at the same time, would be together in \(r\) hours if they traveled in the same direction, but would pass each other in \(t\) hours if they traveled in opposite directions. The ratio of the speed of the faster cyclist to that of the slower is:

solutions.text:
Let the speeds be \(u\gt v.\) The two meeting conditions give \[ u-v=\frac kr,\qquad u+v=\frac kt. \] Adding and subtracting these equations yields \[ \begin{aligned} u&=\frac k2\left(\frac1r+\frac1t\right),\\ v&=\frac k2\left(\frac1t-\frac1r\right). \end{aligned} \] Therefore \[ \frac uv=\frac{r+t}{r-t}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let the faster and slower speeds be \(u\) and \(v\), and write the same-direction and opposite-direction relative-speed equations
